correctness.rationale: From A²=−ρ²I, a norm-attaining unit e_1 has e_2=Ae_1/a of unit norm and Ae_2=−(ρ²/a)e_1. The general lower bound ||Av||≥ρ²/a on unit vectors is attained at e_2. For a>b the two vectors are orthogonal as singular vectors for distinct extrema, and for a=b they are orthogonal by the antiunitary square identity. Thus M=[[0,−b],[a,0]] is a valid unitary canonical form. With the inner product linear first, y=conj(q)x+k exp(iφ)(−conj(x_2),conj(x_1)). Writing z=2|x_1|²−1, the phase extrema at fixed z are the sum and absolute difference of |q|(a−b)√(1−z²)/2 and k[(a+b)+(a−b)z]/2. Their global extrema follow by optimizing kz±|q|√(1−z²) and, when the signed difference changes sign, by continuity. The compact connected domain of constrained pairs and simultaneous phase rotation give every intermediate modulus and its whole circle. This checks the zero threshold by squaring, both endpoint regimes, the equal-singular-value circle and the radii 1/2 and 7/2 in the example. The supporting script was inspected but not executed; a finite diagnostic is not evidence for all constrained pairs.

evidence: Use the unitary with columns (1,1)/√2 and i(1,−1)/√2. It Takagi-diagonalizes the symmetric part of B to diag(δ,δ); the skew coefficient becomes −iγ because the determinant is −i.

The ellipse then has horizontal semiaxis |q|δ and vertical semiaxis δ. Its center-to-origin translation is along the vertical axis with magnitude kγ. The ellipse lies in the radius-δ disk and contains the entire vertical segment from −iδ to iδ. Thus the distance minimum and maximum to the translation point are [kγ−δ]_+ and kγ+δ, including degenerate ellipses.
The inequality for zero membership is exactly kγ≤δ, or |q|≥2√(ab)/(a+b).
